neighbours.label: the token just before the members of a counted, known set that the items map onto one-to-one ('represent | the seven days', 'one for each | of the colonies', 'clearly | the twelve apostles')
fire: The six points of the star stand for the six days of work.
On the shield, four lions represent the four provinces of the kingdom.
There are fifty stars on the banner, one for each state in the union.
The three knots in the cord symbolize the three vows of the order.
The eight spokes of the wheel represent the eight steps of the path.
Count the candles on the table: they are obviously the seven virtues.
The ten strings of the harp were said to signify the ten commandments.
She planted twelve trees, one for each month of the year.
quiet: The points of the star were painted gold and silver.
On the shield, a lion represents courage in battle.
There are bright stars on the banner and a wide red border.
The lawyer agreed to represent the tenants at the hearing.
The spokes of the wheel were made of polished oak.
Count the candles on the table and bring more if needed.
The strings of the harp were said to be made of silver.
She planted apple trees along the edge of the field.

short: N things stand for the N members
notes: Card: 'twelve pillars to represent the Twelve Tribes', 'five fingers symbolize the five pillars', 'clearly the twelve apostles', 'one for each year'; the output (reversed for this pole) promotes elements/parts/components/pillars. Probes: 0.99, 0.69, 0.58, 0.88; 'represent the company in court' 0.02. The + pole is the other side: a whole introducing its contents (with:, contain, featuring).
